items.title: Oil hits $100 a barrel for first time since July after US and Houthi strikes
items.description: Brent crude - the global benchmark for prices - rises after the US hit five Iranian tankers on Tuesday

items.title: US to ban imports of some Canadian alcohol, dairy goods and motorbikes
items.description: It is the latest strike in a long trade war, and comes after Canadian counter-tariffs on US goods come into force.

items.title: Tycoon to pay ex-wife $1.87bn in record South Korea divorce settlement
items.description: The billion dollar payout marks the largest divorce settlement in the country's history.

items.title: Meta continues to run ads promoting child sexual abuse material in India - report
items.description: The report follows a BBC Eye investigation that found Instagram running paid ads promoting such material in India.

items.title: Baby orangutans found in Indian forest spark trafficking inquiry
items.description: The critically endangered apes were found far from their natural habitat in the eastern Indian state of Odisha.

items.title: 'You're not alone in the darkness': Gambia president urges calm after violent blackout protests
items.description: The country has faced persistent blackouts since June, with some lasting up to 48 hours, residents say.

items.title: Hong Kong's first leader after British handover dies
items.description: The tenure of Tung Chee-hwa, Hong Kong's first leader after Britain handed over the city to China, was marked by crises and protests.

items.title: Argentina to file criminal case against oil company operating in Falklands
items.description: The move comes days after President Javier Milei stepped up Argentina's claims of sovereignty over the Falklands.

items.title: British widow faces deportation from Sweden after 22 years
items.description: A 78-year-old British woman is facing deportation for failing to fill out a Brexit residence application on time.

items.title: South Park creators rename show 'South America' in apparent dig at Trump
items.description: Since beginning his second term, the US president has said he wanted to use the word 'America' to rename a lake, a gulf and even a US state.

items.title: Ukrainian TV channel building hit by Russian drone as five killed in Kyiv
items.description: President Zelensky describes the daytime drone attack in Ukraine's capital as a "new page in Russian degradation"

items.title: Saudi Arabia vows to respond after Houthis attack cities and energy facilities
items.description: The Iran-backed Yemeni group's attacks have injured 73 people and caused fires at oil facilities, Saudi authorities say.

items.title: Fourteen go on trial over deadliest Channel small boats disaster
items.description: At least 30 men, women and children drowned when their dinghy capsized on 24 November 2021.

items.title: LIV files for bankruptcy protection with over $45m owed to players
items.description: LIV Golf has filed for bankruptcy protection with at least $45m (£33m) owed to players, who will now have the option to leave.

items.title: 'Constantly on my mind' - 9/11 agony endures for bereaved, 25 years on
items.description: As the 25th anniversary approaches, the wait for the alleged mastermind of the attack to be put on trial goes on.

items.title: British-Israeli relations at lowest ebb in decades
items.description: Israel's response to London's trade ban with Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank shows how important this moment is.

items.title: Hegseth is shaking up the Pentagon as the US wages war - but at what cost?
items.description: The upheaval in the military could shape the legacy of Trump's second term, writes the BBC's Tom Bateman.

items.title: A food safety officer has become a social media star in India - why?
items.description: Tukaram Mundhe has gone viral after a series of aggressive inspections of restaurants to detect hygiene lapses.

items.title: AI will cure cancer in our lifetime, claims boss of UK chip giant
items.description: Arm Holding's chief executive Rene Haas says artificial intelligence will find a solution to the disease.

items.title: Where is Israel's proposed West Bank settlement the UK opposes?
items.description: BBC's Middle East correspondent Lucy Williamson reports from an area close to Israel's proposed site in the occupied West Bank.
